correctness.rationale: Let \(\bar S=\Lambda/d_1\). The differentiated delay-compensating functional \(W_0=\Phi(S)+I+\beta\int_{t-\tau_1}^t S(s)I(s)\,ds\) satisfies exactly \(W_0'=-d_1(S-\bar S)^2/S+(\beta\bar S-d_2)I-IQ/(1+I)\); the package symbolic checker reconstructs this cancellation. Adding \(cQ\), with \(c\|h\|_\infty\le1\), and using the age-transport mass balance gives at \(\beta\bar S=d_2\) a nonpositive derivative with coercive dissipation in \(S-\bar S\) and \(Q\). Source boundedness plus an eventual positive lower bound on \(S\) makes the squared susceptible deviation integrable and uniformly continuous, so Barbalat yields \(S\to\bar S\). Bounded \(I\) gives bounded \(\dot I\), hence bounded \(\ddot S\); the derivative form of Barbalat gives \(\dot S\to0\), and the susceptible equation then forces \(I\to0\). The predator mass inequality then gives \(Q\to0\), and the characteristic formulas give the asserted age-profile convergence. This closes the source's strict threshold to the equality without relying on finite simulation.
